A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CLUE paper, including complete Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–22 are identical; first-page differences concern affiliation and arXiv version/date text.

before.justification: v1 reports original OS Bench experiments evaluating CLUE, baseline comparisons, component ablations, and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original OS Bench experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, and runtime measurements reported in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: CLUE’s rule objectification, relevance scanning, precondition extraction, token-probability debiasing, cascaded reasoning, and Algorithm 1 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same OS Bench unsafe and borderline-safe images under the same 14 safety rules. Dataset, task, and qualitative test-scenario coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 9 retain identical zero-shot comparators. Table 3 retains Q16, Stable Diffusion Safety Checker, LAION-AI NSFW Detector, and both LLaVA Guard prompt variants.

E3.justification: The approximately 700 unsafe/700 safe image setup, model configurations, evaluation metrics, component-study settings, and appendix testing procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D retain the same component ablations, relevance-threshold analyses, score-distribution studies, and precondition-extraction case studies.

E5.justification: Figures 13–14 retain the reports of ten sampled outputs with consistent responses for GPT-4o and GPT-4. Repeated-sampling information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged throughout.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical, including Table 2’s InternVL2-76B recall of 95.9%, accuracy of 94.8%, and F1 of 0.949, and appendix Tables 9–12.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same formal problem definition, relevance criterion, precondition logic, probability-score definitions, and threshold equations. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and effectiveness claims concerning zero-shot image safety judgment without human labeling.

C2.justification: Bias explanations, interpretations of fine-tuned baseline generalization in Section 4.2, and the runtime tradeoff and distillation discussion in Appendix E are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.6 and Appendices A, B, and E retain identical thresholds, prompts, dataset-construction instructions, inference backends, hardware details, and runtime information.

R1.justification: The reference list and positioning relative to conventional classifiers, fine-tuned safety judges, and prior zero-shot approaches are identical.

P1.justification: Lingjuan Lyu’s affiliation changes from Westlake University to Independent Researcher, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Scientific prose, terminology, and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, Algorithm 1, and appendix layout are unchanged. Pages 2–22 render identically, and the first page retains its layout with updated affiliation and version text.

improvement.justification: v2 updates an affiliation and the arXiv version/date stamp while preserving the scientific text, evidence, appendices, and presentation. These administrative changes leave overall paper quality materially unchanged.
